item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Excellent, but I have to agree that "a skeleton popped out" isn't really the sort of climax I was hoping for. I think the climax in the main article, all the effected kids being eaten by the great pumpkin, was much better, and something that relates to that would have been a better ending, like all the anomalous entities standing around crying for someone to come out and play with increasing frenzy. Also, a dash of the unknown would be good. The skeletons are too… how do I even say this… to visible, if you understand what I mean. Not that animated skeletons aren't creepy and impossible and whatever, but as a literary device, they're cliche. They would fit better as buildup than climax, since most of the buildup involves Halloween memes brought to life. I loved the bedsheet ghosts, for example. Excellent creepy buildup. The skeleton pumpkins could serve similarly. Still, +1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Hmm… well, that's pretty close to a Universal Receiver (AB+ is slightly better IIRC as Rh-negative people cannot receive Rh-positive blood). Also makes it pretty useless for transfusions since only people with blood type AB can receive the red blood cells (although anyone can receive the plasma). It's also a very rare type, less than 1% for all countries. My bet would be that the rarity is why the author included it.

And yes, the ABO and Rh systems are just two systems for blood matching, but they're close enough for 99% of the cases.

item.content:encoded: 10/27/████ 18:45 Upon review of O'Toole autopsy footage, Dr. King reported the operating table contained only eight apple seeds, which morticians carefully dissected. Audio was likewise said to be affected, replaced with a dramatic narration of the life of one John Chapman, describing his death in inordinate detail. Footage reviewed by security personnel; no anomalies reported. Dr. King transferred to Site ██ for psychiatric evaluation.
